question: As per NITI Aayog's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) - 2021, which state has the highest percentage of people who are poor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per **NITI Aayog's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) - 2021**, **Bihar** has the highest percentage of people living in poverty among all states in India.
 
• The index considers factors like health, education, and standard of living to measure poverty comprehensively.
 
• The **NITI Aayog Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, released in 2021, is a comprehensive measure of poverty that goes beyond income levels.
 
• It considers three broad dimensions—**health, education, and standard of living**—and evaluates multiple indicators under each dimension.
 
• The index aligns with the methodology of the global MPI developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• Bihar was reported to have the highest percentage of people in poverty, with **51.91%** of its population being multidimensionally poor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jharkhand** ranks second, with **42.16%** of its population being multidimensionally poor.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** follows, with **37.79%** of its population living in poverty.
 
• States like **Tamil Nadu** and **Telangana** have much lower poverty percentages, thanks to better performance in health, education, and infrastructure.
